Relative URLs in Web Performance

By Jane Doe

Relative URLs let browsers resolve asset paths against the current page location, which keeps deployments portable across staging and production. This article explains how to reason about them safely.

Why base paths matter

Every resource address is resolved against baseURI. When a page is served from a subdirectory, naive relative links can silently break.

  • Use absolute paths for critical assets.
  • Keep loading="lazy" images with a real fallback source.

A stable URL is a contract between the author and the reader.
